background: In May 2013, the Russian-language hacking forum YouHack suffered a data breach that was later redistributed as part of a larger corpus of data . The breach exposed 107k forum members' email addresses, usernames, IP addresses and MD5 password hashes, most of which were unsalted. Forum posts also contained email address and password pairs belonging to other victims, bringing the total to 7.2M unique email addresses.
how: The published account does not explain the exact way the data was obtained.
outcome: 7,160,849 accounts are listed in this breach. This is a count of accounts, not necessarily individual people.
The reported exposed data includes Email addresses, IP addresses, Passwords, Usernames.

fields.name: Passwords
fields.why: Anyone reusing this password elsewhere has those accounts exposed too, credential stuffing is automated and tries them all within days.

fields.name: IP addresses
fields.why: Approximate location at the time of use, and a way to correlate accounts across services.

fields.name: Email addresses
fields.why: An exposed address may be used in phishing attempts. Treat unexpected messages with caution.

fields.name: Usernames
fields.why: A matching handle can be a lead to other profiles, but does not prove shared ownership.

actions: Change this password anywhere you reused it, starting with your email account, that is the one that can reset all the others.
Be alert to phishing. A message may use details from exposed or collected records to appear familiar; verify requests through the service directly.

background: In March 2023, data allegedly taken from СберСпасибо (SberSpasibo), the loyalty program of Russian bank Сбербанк (Sberbank), was published online . The data contained records relating to 48M users, including 3.3M unique email addresses alongside phone numbers and dates of birth. Data also included bank card numbers stored as unsalted SHA-1 hashes, plus loyalty program details such as membership dates and the redemption of bonus points for partner offers.
how: The published account does not explain the exact way the data was obtained.
outcome: 3,288,711 accounts are listed in this breach. This is a count of accounts, not necessarily individual people.
The reported exposed data includes Bank card numbers, Dates of birth, Email addresses, Loyalty program details, Phone numbers.

background: In November 2025, Harvard University suffered a data breach later linked to a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion attempt . The data contained 851k unique email addresses relating to the university's alumni and fundraising systems, along with extensive profile information for donors, alumni, parents and some faculty, staff and students.

In Harvard's disclosure notice , the university stated that the breach impacted "personal information such as email addresses, telephone numbers, home and business addresses, event attendance, details of donations to the University, and other biographical information pertaining to University fundraising and alumni engagement activities".
how: The published account does not explain the exact way the data was obtained.
motive: In November 2025, Harvard University suffered a data breach later linked to a ShinyHunters "pay or leak" extortion attempt .
outcome: 850,537 accounts are listed in this breach. This is a count of accounts, not necessarily individual people.

background: In September 2026, the German political party Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) suffered a data breach which exposed 345k unique email addresses. The following month, hundreds of gigabytes of data containing hundreds of thousands of emails and attachments was published online, with searchable AI-generated summaries and downloadable original files.

An analysis of the incident reported that the breach was detected as early as 9 September, with a subsequent intrusion occurring five days later. In its public statement , AfD attributed the breach to an attack on a hosting provider, identified in subsequent reporting as the party-owned Alternita Dienstleistungs GmbH.
how: The published account does not explain the exact way the data was obtained.
outcome: 345,439 accounts are listed in this breach. This is a count of accounts, not necessarily individual people.
The reported exposed data includes Email addresses, Email messages.
